title: openai-chat-completions-parity: streaming roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting & function-calls
author: Tom Nguyen
release_notes: Adds parity for OpenAI /v1/chat.completions: streaming stability for roles, stop and logprobs behavior, improved response formatting and function-call semantics. Backwards compatible with existing Redwood API; opt-in via compat flag.
description: Motivation: implement parity with OpenAI /v1/chat.completions to make Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer behave identically for streaming outputs, role handling, stop sequences, logprobs, response formatting, and function/tool calling. This change addresses customer reports about subtle differences in streaming chunk boundaries and function call emission under high-concurrency workloads (SUP-983) and unifies behavior for downstream SDKs and the hosted API. What this PR does: 1) Streaming stability: stabilize chunk boundaries by aligning flush conditions to OpenAI semantics (tokens, eos, role-change deltas), add guards for partial token emission under batching, and add an opt-in compatibility flag to revert to legacy behavior. 2) Roles & metadata: ensure message-level role attribution (system/user/assistant/tool) is preserved across stream fragments and in final delta patches. 3) Stop sequences & logprobs: honor multiple stop tokens during streaming, compute and attach token-level logprobs on final output only, and ensure stop-truncation is consistent with OpenAI edge cases. 4) Response formatting: normalize whitespace and JSON-structured outputs to avoid double-escaping when using structured_output and function calling; add a canonical formatter and tests. 5) Function/tool calling: emit function call events as a single atomic frame when detected; support both streaming and non-streaming function call styles compatible with OpenAI clients. Implementation highlights: updates to src/api/compat/openai_chat_completions.rs (core compatibility layer), changes in serving/runtime/streaming.rs to add new flush heuristics, KV cache adjustments to prevent premature token reveals, integrations in python/ and typescript/ SDKs to expose the compat flag, and extensive tests and e2e harness updates under test/integration/openai_parity. Checklist: - [x] Implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration tests against OpenAI parity harness - [x] SDK bindings updated (python + typescript) - [x] Docs updated (redwood-docs/openai_compat.md) - [x] Performance smoke tests and CI green - [x] Release notes drafted Related: ENG-4123 (streaming stability), ENG-4178 (function call parity), SUP-983 (customer incident).

notes_for_reviewers: This PR intentionally keeps the compat flag opt-in. If customers request default parity, follow-up will be an ops-safe rollout with feature gating and telemetry.
egress_considerations: No user data exfiltration changes. Ensure KMS keys unchanged for private deployments.
testing_summary: Added 28 unit tests, 6 integration scenarios against the OpenAI parity harness, and smoke perf runs. Integration harness compares streaming chunk sequences and final messages against a golden OpenAI reference. CI pipeline includes a dedicated openai_parity job.
backcompat_strategy: Default behavior unchanged; enable parity via request header 'X-OpenAI-Compat: 1' or per-project setting in Console. SDKs expose a compat=true flag in client constructors.
observability_changes: Added metrics: compat.openai.stream.chunks, compat.openai.function_calls.count, compat.openai.stop_truncations and tracing span openai_compat_parity.* to help correlate regressions.
security_implications: No new auth surfaces. Function call events are logged at INFO and can be redacted by existing payload-scrubbing hooks.
